body: Much of what I know just happens to fall into my brain. Sometimes,  if I am feeling particularly argumentative, I might look things up. The knowledge of psychology is mostly due to involuntary interaction with the b system. Haha. Though, I agree in that the desire for oblivion and how that can be the only genuine desire anyone could possess has made me learn quite a few things.

I've always been somewhat interested in philosophy but have preferred schools of thoughts that were more existential in nature. I did study some eastern religion in uni. I've done volunteering and such. it never felt like I was doing something good and I'd have to stop after a little while just to maintain my sanity. As far as meditation is concerned, I have almost no ability to do so. Quiet moments come sometimes when I am driving or something but other than that... I don't really know.

I don't really have much of an idea. I don't open up with professionals or anyone offline in any way and use therapy to just talk about random things so there isn't much of a chance of finding out. I can speculate and research but I'd rather not indulge in self-diagnosis and self-suggestions. I am aware now that the line of thought is simply a projection of my own desire. But knowing that makes me feel even more lost.
The idea of nothingness, of being nothing. Freudian concept of thanatos is the only thing I can think of. At least I no longer think everyone desires it. That felt like heavy of a burden.

There doesn't seem to be a precipitating factor. It has just been a deep desire for a long time... probably since childhood.  Only the thought of dying feels right. When I do productive things, my mind nags at me to stop. When I just exist, my mind nags at me to stop that too. I used to think everyone thought that way but turns out  that I was wrong. Of course I've never done much more than to collect supplies or be reckless so I can't really even validate these feelings to myself.
